comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C25-C43) about Lrp4 alleles and NMJ development. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED, concluding that membrane anchoring is required for postnatal maturation. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, arguing that the conclusion about maturation is a 'misinterpretation' since many maturation events (synapse elimination, γ-ε subunit switch) appear normal in Lrp4ECD/ECD mice. Reviewers distinguish between impaired growth and impaired maturation.

Both evaluate genetic epistasis claims (C48-C54, C95). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance and synergistic phenotypes. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the genetic interaction but questioning whether the phenotypic differences are 'sufficiently robust' and requesting additional quantitative analysis to demonstrate that the double mutant 'significantly affects postsynaptic differentiation.'

Both evaluate APP-LRP4 physical interaction claims (C21, C56-C57, C59, C93). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergence of multiple experimental approaches (pull-down, cell aggregation). Peer reviewers explicitly state the demonstration is 'strong and convincing,' though they request additional experiments to demonstrate functional necessity.

Both evaluate the preformed LRP4-APP-MuSK complex claim (C75). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and efficient immunodepletion. Peer reviewers do not challenge the co-immunoprecipitation data, though they request additional experiments on functional necessity.

Both evaluate prepatterning claims (C84-C86). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED, noting that initial prepatterning does not require APP/APLP2. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting additional analysis of prepatterning in APP-/- and APLP2-/- mice, suggesting current data may be insufficient to fully address APP's role in prepatterning.

Both evaluate APP-agrin binding claims (C22, C76-C77, C82-C83, C94). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the APP-agrin interaction is direct or mediated through other factors, noting that C2C12 cells express muscle agrin and suggesting experiments in agrin-/- conditions. Peer review also includes claims C78-C81 about biphasic effects.

OpenEval R5 evaluates AChR clustering claims (C60-C66) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R5 evaluates overlapping claims (C60-C66) plus MuSK phosphorylation claims (C23, C67-C74, C96) and rates them UNSUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly challenge the conclusion that APP-LRP4 can activate MuSK in the absence of agrin, stating C2C12 cells express muscle agrin. They also question whether RAP-Fc actually binds LRP4.

OpenEval R6 evaluates MuSK phosphorylation claims (C67-C72, C23, C96) and finds them SUPPORTED with quantitative dose-response data. Peer R5 evaluates overlapping claims (C23, C67-C72, C96) plus AChR clustering claims (C60-C66, C73-C74) and rates them UNSUPPORTED, challenging the conclusion that APP-LRP4 can activate MuSK without agrin due to endogenous agrin expression in C2C12 cells.

OpenEval R7 evaluates claims (C73-C74) about APP functioning through LRP4 and MuSK using knockout myotubes and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R5 includes these claims in a broader evaluation (C23, C60-C74, C96) rated UNSUPPORTED, challenging the overall conclusion about APP's ability to activate MuSK independently of agrin.

OpenEval R9 evaluates biphasic agrin effects on LRP4-APP interaction (C78-C81, C24, C97) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes some overlapping claims (C78-C81) along with APP-agrin binding claims (C22, C76-C77, C82-C83, C94) and rates them UNCERTAIN, questioning whether APP-agrin interaction is direct or mediated through other factors.

Both evaluate LRP4 localization claims (C87-C90). OpenEval R11 also includes C91-C92 and finds all SUPPORTED, documenting developmental time course and reduced LRP4 at NMJ despite increased total expression. Peer R8 rates this UNCERTAIN, requesting more comprehensive developmental expression profiles of APP and LRP4 in both motoneurons and muscles.

OpenEval R11 evaluates LRP4 localization and expression claims (C87-C92) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R9 evaluates only the compensatory upregulation claims (C91-C92) and finds them SUPPORTED. Both agree on the increased LRP4 expression in Lrp4ECD/ECD muscle.

OpenEval R12 evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C20, C46-C47, C55, C58, C98-C114) from prior literature and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval R13 evaluates background claims (C44-C45) about continuous MuSK activity from prior work (Hesser et al., 2006) and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
